examples.text: Wie würden sie als Fachleute die Situation bewerten?
examples.translation: Jak oni oceniliby tę sytuację jako specjaliści?

glosses: Évaluer.

examples.text: Um seine Mittel effizient einzusetzen, hat der Bund die ihm unterbreiteten Agglomerationsprogramme anhand der vier gesetzlich vorgegebenen Kriterien nach deren Wirkung bewertet: Die Programme sollen die Qualität des Verkehrssystems verbessern, die Siedlungsentwicklung nach innen fördern, die Verkehrssicherheit erhöhen sowie die Umweltbelastung und den Ressourcenverbrauch senken.
examples.translation: Pour assurer l’utilisation efficace de ses moyens, la Confédération a évalué l’effet des projets d’agglomération qui lui ont été soumis selon les quatre critères prescrits par la loi : les programmes doivent améliorer la qualité du système de transport, développer l’urbanisation à l’intérieur du tissu bâti, accroître la sécurité du trafic et réduire les atteintes à l’environnement et l’utilisation des ressources.

glosses: Estimer la valeur.

examples.text: Das Unternehmen wird an der Börse mit 20 Milliarden Dollar bewertet.

examples.text: Since element (15.1) evaluates to an element of the center in any alternative algebra, (15.1) has to evaluate to a scalar multiple of the identity element of the Cayley-Dickson algebra.
In one type of such an integral, the integrand is only the probability density function, and the integral evaluates to a probability, which of course is a scalar.

glosses: The worth of something; value.

examples.text: There shall no figure at such rate be set, / As that of true and faithfull Iuliet.
His natural parts were not of the first rate, but he had greatly improved them by a learned education.

glosses: The proportional relationship between one amount, value etc. and another.

examples.text: At the height of his powers, he was producing pictures at the rate of four a year.

And for online adverts the “conversion” into sales was a minuscule 0.01%.

glosses: Speed.

examples.text: The car was speeding down here at a hell of a rate.
Many of the horse could not march at that rate, nor come up soon enough.

glosses: The relative speed of change or progress.

examples.text: The rate of production at the factory is skyrocketing.

glosses: The price of (an individual) thing; cost.

examples.text: He asked quite a rate to take me to the airport.

glosses: A set price or charge for all examples of a given case, commodity, service etc.

examples.text: Postal rates here are low.

glosses: A wage calculated in relation to a unit of time.

examples.text: We pay an hourly rate of between $10 – $15 per hour depending on qualifications and experience.

glosses: Any of various taxes, especially those levied by a local authority.

examples.text: I hardly have enough left every month to pay the rates.

glosses: A class into which ships were assigned based on condition, size etc.; by extension, rank.

examples.text: This textbook is first-rate.

glosses: Established portion or measure; fixed allowance; ration.

examples.text: The one right feeble through the evil rate / Of food which in her duress she had found.

glosses: Order; arrangement.

examples.text: Thus sat they all around in seemly rate.

glosses: Ratification; approval.

examples.text:
c. 1610s, George Chapman, Caesar and Pompey
Tis offerd, Sir, 'boue the rate of Caesar
In other men, but in what I approue
Beneath his merits: which I will not faile
T'enforce at full to Pompey, nor forget
In any time the gratitude of my seruice.

glosses: The gain or loss of a timepiece in a unit of time.

examples.text: daily rate; hourly rate; etc.

glosses: To assign or be assigned a particular rank or level.

examples.text: She is rated fourth in the country.

glosses: To evaluate or estimate the value of.

examples.text: They rate his talents highly.

glosses: To consider or regard.

examples.text: He rated this book brilliant.

glosses: To deserve; to be worth.

glosses: To determine the limits of safe functioning for a machine or electrical device.

examples.text: The transformer is rated at 10 watts.

glosses: To evaluate a property's value for the purposes of local taxation.

examples.text: The customers don't rate the new burgers.

examples.text: Throughout the first turn is where the jockey rates the horse if the need arises. Rating a horse is where you keep it from putting out too much too soon.

glosses: To have position (in a certain class).

examples.text: He rates as the best cyclist in the country.

glosses: To have value or standing.

examples.text: This last performance of hers didn't rate very high with the judges.

glosses: To ratify.

examples.text: to rate the truce

glosses: To ascertain the exact rate of the gain or loss of (a chronometer) as compared with true time.

Andronicus the Emperour, finding by chance in his pallace certaine principall men very earnestly disputing against Lapodius about one of our points of great importance, taunted and rated them very bitterly, and threatened if they gave not over, he would cause them to be cast into the river.
So when he aroſe, he getteth him a grievous Crab-tree cudgel, and goes down into the Dungeon to them; and there firſt falls to Rateing of them, as if they were dogs: [...]

The successful monk, on the morrow morning, hastens home to Ely [...]. The successful monk, arriving at Ely, is rated for a goose and an owl; is ordered back to say that Elmset was the place meant.

glosses: To cause (hay, hemp, flax, etc) to decay (whether in an injurious way, or—as retting—in a useful way) by exposure to weather, particularly wetness.

examples.text: From the "line pit" it [flax] is carried to the “RATING GROUND;" - a piece of unbroken aftergrass, where the sheaflets are untied, and the flax spread thin upon the grass. It is calculated, that a full crop ought to cover as much ground as it grew upon. Here it lies until it be sufficiently "rated;" namely, until the more woodlike substance of the stems will separate […]

[…] hay when it is cocked either wette or greene, for then sure it is to be rated, and beinge rated looseth both the goode smell and goode taste; and likewise the colour, as yow may perceive by the blackenesse of the cocke on the outside; for if the[…]
